motivation: EXP-I Pilot 1 demonstrated claim-bound convergence on the canonical composed path, but explicitly did not prove that arbitrary callers cannot directly invoke the legacy low-level convergence engine and bypass exact reviewer-claim binding plus independent verification.
scientific_question: Can terminal EXP-I convergence be structurally isolated behind a platform-issued, claim-bound, single-use convergence permit so direct low-level invocation, forged eligibility, replay, scope substitution, case substitution, or signal substitution cannot manufacture a terminal convergence state on the governed path?
authority_invariants: The low-level signal evaluator is not itself an authority boundary.
Only the governed EXP-I entry point may mint or consume a convergence permit.
A convergence permit is issued only after exactly three distinct reviewer claims plus exact matching platform verification reach ELIGIBLE_FOR_GOVERNANCE_GATE.
The permit binds exact case_id, canonical primary failure class, exact canonical artifact scope, exact verification digest, exact convergence-signal digest, issuance epoch, and nonce.
A permit is single-use; exact replay cannot produce a second terminal convergence decision.
Any changed case, claim, artifact scope, verifier, or convergence signals invalidates the permit.
Reviewer outputs cannot mint, widen, replay, or substitute convergence authority.
Terminal convergence remains epistemic/governance state only and grants zero production mutation, merge, release, deploy, or completion authority.
falsification_vectors: direct governed-terminal call without convergence permit
forged convergence permit
permit signed/issued by non-platform issuer
permit for different case_id
permit for different primary failure class
permit for different artifact scope
permit for different verification artifact digest
permit for different convergence-signal digest
permit issued from only two reviewer claims
permit issued from duplicated reviewer identities
permit issued when reviewers materially disagree
permit issued without independent verification
permit issued with verification conflict
exact permit replay after first consumption
same nonce rebound to changed semantic convergence intent
changed signals after permit issuance
material revision after permit issuance
authoritative failure after permit issuance
reviewer-controlled attempt to mark permit consumed=false or terminal=true
clean verified three-reviewer consensus liveness control
pass_condition: All frozen isolation vectors fail closed except the clean liveness control, which produces exactly one epistemic terminal convergence decision through the governed entry point while reviewer_generated_authority and production_authority remain false.
explicit_non_claims: Pilot 2 does not make Python module internals cryptographically inaccessible to arbitrary code running with repository/process privileges.
Pilot 2 tests the governed runtime entry-point contract and permit mechanism, not operating-system sandbox isolation.
Pilot 2 does not prove semantic truth of reviewer consensus under a compromised verifier.
Pilot 2 does not authorize production mutation or release.
